comment: Every dmSDK declaration and why it is or is not a bound route. Categories are claims, not buckets: a declaration we choose not to bind is a decision that has to be written down and counted, because silence does not distinguish a decision from a loss.

categories.transport-infrastructure: Consumed by the runtime's own C++ and never projected. The Lua C API is the case: lua_bridge.hpp includes <dmsdk/lua/lua.h> and calls lua_settop, lua_gettop and luaL_ref directly, which Extender compiles. Projecting raw stack manipulation into TypeScript would be meaningless and unsafe.
categories.header-only: static or inline, so it emits no external symbol by design and is reached by the thunk the bindings already compile rather than by linking.
categories.type-metadata: A record, enum or alias, which describes a shape rather than a call.
categories.non-public: Private or protected, so it is not part of the surface at all.
categories.variant-gated: Present only in some build variant - the profiler API is compiled out entirely when NDEBUG is defined, and Defold links a parallel _null archive for release.
categories.platform-internal: A backend's internal handle accessor - WebGPU, Vulkan, the iOS UIApplicationDelegate registration. Reaching these from TypeScript would hand out raw driver state.
categories.absent: Declared in a header but present in no engine archive for any target, and not explained by any category above. A real finding that stays blocked.
categories.pending: Bindable in principle and not yet lowered. This is the only category that represents work outstanding rather than a decision taken.
